case-1.objects: Two measurable spaces A and B; two probability measures mu and nu on A; one common Markov kernel K from A to B; a real tolerance delta; and the two composed measures K o_m mu and K o_m nu on B.
case-1.domains: A and B are arbitrary types equipped with measurable-space structures. The input events s are measurable subsets of A, and the output events t are measurable subsets of B. The kernel assigns measures on B to points of A. The compared event masses and delta are real numbers.
case-1.quantifiers: Universally, for implicit types A and B and their measurable-space instances, for measures mu and nu on A with probability instances, for K : Kernel A B with a Markov instance, and for implicit delta in R: if for every s subset of A, measurability of s implies the input bound, then for every t subset of B, measurability of t implies the output bound. The same mu, nu, K, and delta are fixed throughout those event quantifiers.
case-1.assumptions: A and B carry measurable-space structures; mu and nu are probability measures (each has total mass one); K is a measurable kernel whose assigned measure at every x in A has total mass one; for every measurable s subset of A, |mu.real(s) - nu.real(s)| <= delta. There is no separate delta >= 0 hypothesis; the bound at the empty event implies it.
case-1.conclusion: For every measurable t subset of B, |(K o_m mu).real(t) - (K o_m nu).real(t)| <= delta, using the same K on both input measures and the same tolerance delta as in the hypothesis.
case-1.senses: The differences are absolute differences of real-valued measurable-event masses, not differences in extended nonnegative reals. On a measurable output event t, K o_m rho is evaluated by integrating x -> K(x)(t) against rho and then taking the real event mass. This is non-expansion in the event-supremum convention for total variation, expressed as a uniform eventwise implication. It asserts no equality, strict improvement, pointwise bound between kernel rows, bound on nonmeasurable events, or identity for a differently normalized variation norm.
case-1.constants: The very same real delta bounds both sides of the implication, with coefficient one and no additive loss or other constant. The normalization in the probability-measure and Markov-kernel assumptions is total mass one. No numerical value of delta or strict contraction coefficient is specified.
